Corroboration: Two independent public-domain witnesses were read for every oration: the Pustet Ratisbon 1862 whole-book text layer and the Tours: Mame 1922 editio quarta iuxta typicam Vaticanam (artifact ia-scan-pdf-9873693a), the latter reconstructed column by column from its page word bounding boxes. The Vatican typica 1604 and Venice 1570 were swept but not relied on (both are registered degraded-latin and their records forbid resting a claim on a raw search over them)..

Recorded limitation: || REPAIRED by lane repair-2 on 2026-09-03. The stored target had been a text-layer reading carrying recogniser damage; it has been replaced word for word by a reading taken from the 1962 CMAA facsimile page image at 400 dpi (artifact PDF p. 124, printed folio read on the same image). Line-end hyphens are joined, printed stress accents are dropped, and the ae/oe ligatures are expanded to two letters; punctuation, capitalisation and the conclusion are reproduced at the length the page prints them. The verdict, the antecedent locus and the recorded differences are the original lane's and were not revisited. The marginal number 293 already in the locus was confirmed on the same 400 dpi image. IMPORTANT FOR THE APPLIER: the page reading turns out to be character for character identical to the string that was quarantined, so this row was a FALSE POSITIVE of the damage-family screen and not a damaged reading at all. The token the quarantine note names is ordinary Latin, not recogniser damage: the three-letter adverb in the middle of the petition. Every word was nevertheless read afresh on the 1962 page image at 400 dpi before this was concluded. If the screen is run again unchanged it will refuse this row again for the same reason.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Caelesti lumine, quaesumus, Domine, semper et ubique nos praiveni: ut
mysterium, cujus nos participes esse voluisti, et puro cernamus intuitu, et
digno percipiamus affectu. Per Dominum.
